issues.quote: He said a watch that old should not be carried by a man who cannot wind it.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says nothing about the condition, accuracy, or winding of Félix's watch. It gives only the reading (twenty minutes to nine).
issues.misreading: A solver could take this as the husband implying that Félix's watch was stopped or running slow, so the 8:40 reading might not be the true time. That would change the time of Félix's dinner reading, which the puzzle depends on.

issues.quote: The doctor and I played piquet in the salon. Casimir plays badly, and he cheats only when he is losing
issues.fact: The fact sheet says only "the doctor" played piquet with the narrator and went out for cigars. It never names him.
issues.misreading: The transcript never says the doctor is Casimir Vauthier. The link is only implied by context. A careful solver could ask whether the 'he' who left the cards is the same person as Casimir, and the identity is not established by the sheet.

issues.quote: They quarrelled about the price of the repeater.
issues.fact: The fact sheet does not mention a repeater watch or any quarrel. A repeater is a watch that chimes the time on demand.
issues.misreading: The word 'repeater' suggests a watch that can strike the hour, which is a clock-reading hint not on the sheet. A solver might read it as a way to check time at the table, or as a clue about whose watch it is.
